items.title: Tensor fields of type (r,s) on a Lorentzian four-manifold and their components
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $r,s\ge0$ be integers.

**(a) Tensors at a point.** For $p\in M$, the tangent space $T_pM$ is the real
vector space of derivations at $p$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]) and the cotangent space is
its algebraic dual, $T_p^*M=(T_pM)^*$
([[def-cotangent-space-and-cotangent-bundle-as-a-disjoint-union]]). A **type
$(r,s)$ tensor at $p$** is a multilinear map

$$T_p:(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\longrightarrow\mathbb R,$$

in the sense of [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]:
the first $r$ arguments are covectors and the last $s$ are vectors. In
particular a type $(1,0)$ tensor is a vector, a type $(0,1)$ tensor is a
covector and a type $(0,2)$ tensor is a bilinear form, so the covariant
$2$-tensors of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are exactly the
type $(0,2)$ tensors of this definition.

**(b) The tensor bundle and smooth fields.** The **type $(r,s)$ tensor bundle**
$T^r_sM$ is the disjoint union of the fibres $T^r_sM|_p=\operatorname{Mult}((T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s,\mathbb R)$
over $p\in M$ ([[def-type-r-s-tensor-bundle]]); it carries the smooth
vector-bundle structure defined by the tensor-coordinate change rules
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]). A **smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$** on $M$ is a family $T=(T_p)_{p\in M}$ assigning
to each $p$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$, such that for every smooth chart
$(U,x)$ of the maximal smooth atlas the **component functions**

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(q):=T_q\bigl(dx^{a_1}|_q,\dots,dx^{a_r}|_q,\ \partial_{b_1}|_q,\dots,\partial_{b_s}|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

are $C^\infty$ on $U$; here the coordinate derivations
$\partial_b|_q=\partial/\partial x^b|_q$ form a basis of $T_qM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]) and the
coordinate differentials $dx^a|_q$ form the dual basis of $T_q^*M$
([[thm-coordinate-differentials-form-the-dual-cotangent-basis]]). This is
equivalent to $T$ being a smooth section of $T^r_sM$ in the sense of
[[def-smooth-tensor-field]]: the component functions are the frame
coefficients of the section in the local frame induced by the chart. The
smoothness condition is independent of the chosen smooth atlas and the
components in two overlapping charts are related by the transformation law
proved in the lemma on this page; the definition is therefore chart
independent rather than merely chart-wise.

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices are written $a,b,c,\dots$ for components in
a chart, with the Einstein summation convention: a repeated index, once upper
and once lower, is summed over $0,1,2,3$. An upper index is a contravariant
slot in which a covector is evaluated, a lower index a covariant slot in which
a vector is evaluated. Slots are moved between these positions with the
musical isomorphisms $\flat_p,\sharp_p$ of
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]; for example, lowering the
first slot of a type $(1,1)$ field uses $(g^\flat T)^a{}_b=g_{ac}T^c{}_b$ and
raising uses $g^{ac}$. This is an identification of slots, not a change of the
field into a field of another kind, and it uses the metric nondegeneracy.

**(d) Scope.** The definition is purely local and chart-based; no global
triviality of $T^r_sM$, no global frame and no choice of metric-compatible
fields is assumed or implied. All fields are smooth ($C^\infty$); no
lower-regularity or distributional tensor field is defined here. The smooth
structure of the tangent bundle, and hence of $T^r_sM$
([[thm-tensor-transition-laws-define-a-smooth-vector-bundle]]), inherits the
axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] recorded with
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the component formulation of smoothness
itself makes no choice.
items.strategy: Define type (r,s) tensor fields by chart components over the maximal atlas, with the tensor-bundle formulation recorded and index conventions fixed; chart independence and the component law are proved in the companion lemma, and contraction in the next.

items.title: Observers, rest spaces and the spatial projection at an event
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.
items.strategy: Define observers as future-directed unit timelike vectors, rest spaces as orthogonal complements and the spatial projection by its formula; existence is by normalizing the time-orientation field, and the structural properties are proved in the companion lemma.

items.title: Observer congruences, their observer curves and adapted charts
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty
open subset, carrying the restricted smooth structure of
[[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]].

**(a) Congruences.** An **observer congruence** on $U$ is a smooth vector field
$n$ on $U$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) such that
$n_q$ is an observer at $q$ for every $q\in U$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]); explicitly,

$$g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1\quad\text{and}\quad g_q(n_q,N_q)<0\qquad\text{for every }q\in U .$$

Since $g_q(n_q,n_q)=-1$, the field $n$ is nowhere vanishing. A single observer
at a point is therefore not a congruence, and a congruence is not an ordered
basis or frame of $T_qM$.

**(b) Observer curves.** Because $n$ is a smooth vector field on $U$, the
theorem on maximal integral curves
([[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]],
[[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]) assigns to every $q\in U$ a unique
maximal integral curve $\gamma_q:I_q\to U$ of $n$ with $\gamma_q(0)=q$,
defined on an open interval $I_q\subseteq\mathbb R$. We call these curves the
**observers** (or **observer curves**) of the congruence. Each observer is
regular: $\gamma_q'(s)=n_{\gamma_q(s)}$ and $\lVert n\rVert_g=1$ at every
parameter value, so the tangent vector is unit timelike and future-directed at
every parameter value. Completeness of the maximal intervals $I_q$, and global
product or foliation structure of $U$, are not asserted. The parameter $s$ is
the flow parameter of $n$; it is not identified with any clock reading here.

**(c) Adapted charts.** An **$n$-adapted chart** is a smooth chart
$(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3):U'\to\mathbb R^4$ of $M$ whose domain $U'$ is a nonempty
open subset of $U$ and whose **spatial coordinates** $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are constant
along every integral curve of $n$ contained in $U'$; equivalently, for every
$q\in U'$ the observer curve $\gamma_q$ satisfies
$u^i(\gamma_q(s))=u^i(q)$ for all $s$ with $\gamma_q(s)\in U'$ and
$i=1,2,3$. No global adapted chart, and no adapted chart on all of $U$, is
asserted by this definition; one exists near every point of $U$ by the
existence corollary proved on this page.

**(d) Scope.** A congruence is a field of observer directions on an open set; it
is not a chart, not a tetrad field, and not a family of parametrized
worldlines with specified domains. The physical reading of its observer curves
as ideal-clock worldlines, and the identification of the flow parameter with a
measurable time, belong to the physical postulates of the framework and are not
asserted here.
items.strategy: Define congruences as smooth future unit timelike fields, identify their observers as the maximal integral curves, and define adapted charts by constancy of the spatial coordinates along those curves; existence is proved separately.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'worldlines' and 'proper time' on the parametrized curves of particles and their four-velocities, printed pp. 25-27 (PDF pp. 32-34)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 1.9: the definition of an integral curve and the unique integral curve through each point, printed pp. 21-22 (PDF pp. 22-23)

items.title: The component transformation law of a smooth tensor field
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $r,s\ge0$, and let $T$ be a family
assigning to each $p\in M$ a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]). Let $(U,x)$ and $(V,y)$ be
overlapping smooth charts, and write $T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$ and
$T'^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$ for the components of $T$ in the charts
$x$ and $y$. Then for every $q\in U\cap V$,

$$T'^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}(y(q))=\sum_{c_1,\dots,c_r}\sum_{d_1,\dots,d_s}\left(\prod_{i=1}^{r}\frac{\partial y^{a_i}}{\partial x^{c_i}}(x(q))\right)\left(\prod_{j=1}^{s}\frac{\partial x^{d_j}}{\partial y^{b_j}}(y(q))\right)T^{c_1\cdots c_r}{}_{d_1\cdots d_s}(x(q)),$$

where $\partial y^{a}/\partial x^{c}$ and $\partial x^{d}/\partial y^{b}$ are
the entries of the total derivatives of $y\circ x^{-1}$ and $x\circ y^{-1}$.
Moreover $T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r,s)$ if and only if its
components are $C^\infty$ in the charts of some one smooth atlas of $M$; in
that case the components in every smooth chart are $C^\infty$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the multilinear tensor pointwise on the coordinate frames of two overlapping charts, expand each slot with the tangent-basis and dual-basis laws, and use C-infinity closure to transfer smoothness between atlases.

references.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 12 'Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds', printed pp. 316-324
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2 'the tensor transformation law' and 'partial derivatives are not tensors', printed pp. 46-47 (PDF pp. 53-54)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 1.6-1.8 on tensor components and the change of coordinate bases, printed pp. 15-21 (PDF pp. 16-22)

items.title: Contraction of a smooth tensor field is a smooth tensor field
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), let $r,s\ge1$, and let $T$ be a smooth
tensor field of type $(r,s)$ on $M$
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]). For each $p\in M$ let
$(\operatorname{ctr}T)_p$ be the contraction of $T_p$ over its first
contravariant slot and its first covariant slot
([[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Then:

1. $\operatorname{ctr}T$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(r-1,s-1)$ on $M$,
   and its definition is independent of every basis.
2. In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ the components of $\operatorname{ctr}T$ are

   $$(\operatorname{ctr}T)^{a_2\cdots a_r}{}_{b_2\cdots b_s}=\sum_{i=0}^{3}T^{i\,a_2\cdots a_r}{}_{i\,b_2\cdots b_s},$$

   and the field obtained by contracting any other pair consisting of one
   contravariant and one covariant slot has the analogous component formula
   after permuting the slots.
3. If $r=s=1$, then $\operatorname{tr}T:=\operatorname{ctr}T$ is a smooth
   function on $M$ and $\operatorname{tr}T=\sum_{i=0}^{3}T^i{}_i$ in every
   smooth chart.
items.strategy: Define contraction pointwise with the basis-independent mixed-tensor formula and compute its components in the coordinate basis; finite sums of smooth component functions give smoothness in every chart.

references.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 12 'Multilinear Algebra': contraction of tensors, printed pp. 305-313
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'index manipulation': contraction sums over one upper and one lower index (printed p. 17; PDF p. 24)

items.title: The observer rest-space decomposition and the spatial projection
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.
items.strategy: direct

items.title: Pairing of an observer with future causal vectors
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). For $w\in T_pM$ write
$h=h_n$ and $\gamma(w):=-g_p(n,w)$.

1. If $w$ is nonzero future causal, then $\gamma(w)>0$.
2. If $w$ is future unit timelike, then $\gamma(w)\ge1$, with
   $\gamma(w)=1$ if and only if $w=n$, and
   $g_p(h(w),h(w))=\gamma(w)^2-1$.
3. If $w$ is unit timelike, then $w$ is future-directed if and only if
   $g_p(n,w)<0$, and past-directed if and only if $g_p(n,w)>0$; in particular
   $g_p(n,w)\neq0$ for such $w$.
items.strategy: Work in an orthonormal basis with future first vector, compare the observer pairing with the coordinate description of the future cone, and use the projection identity and positive definiteness to get gamma greater or equal 1 and the future/past criterion.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.2 Lorentzian signature: causal vectors at a point fall into two disconnected sets (the light cone), printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'the light cone' (printed p. 7; PDF p. 14) and the classification of vectors as timelike, lightlike or spacelike (printed pp. 15-16; PDF pp. 22-23)

items.title: Local frame fields, coordinate frames and tetrad fields
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Write
$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ for the four-by-four diagonal matrix with
diagonal entries $-1,1,1,1$, and use capital indices $A,B=0,1,2,3$ for frame
members.

**(a) Local frame fields.** A **local frame field** on $U$ is a tuple
$E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of smooth vector fields on $U$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) such that for every
$q\in U$ the vectors $E_0(q),E_1(q),E_2(q),E_3(q)$ form an ordered basis of
$T_qM$, equivalently a pointwise independent tuple of four vector fields.

**(b) Coordinate frames.** If $(U,x)$ is a smooth chart, the tuple
$(\partial/\partial x^0,\partial/\partial x^1,\partial/\partial x^2,\partial/\partial x^3)$
of coordinate fields is a local frame field on $U$, its **coordinate frame**.
Two coordinate fields of one chart commute: by the coordinate formula for the
Lie bracket ([[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]],
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]) applied to constant coordinate
components, $[\partial/\partial x^a,\partial/\partial x^b]=0$ for all $a,b$.
Consequently a local frame field $(E_0,\dots,E_3)$ with $[E_A,E_B]\neq0$ for
some $A,B$ is not the coordinate frame of any chart; this necessary condition
is the only one asserted here, and no converse is claimed by this definition.

**(c) Tetrad fields.** A **tetrad field** (or **$g$-orthonormal frame field**)
on $U$ is a local frame field $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $U$ such that

$$g_q(E_A(q),E_B(q))=\eta_{AB}\qquad\text{for all }A,B\text{ and all }q\in U .$$

A tetrad field is **future-directed** when in addition $E_0(q)$ is
future-directed for every $q\in U$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]); then
each $E_0(q)$ is an observer at $q$ ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]), so
$E_0$ is an observer congruence on $U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]), while $E_1,E_2,E_3$ are pointwise an
orthonormal basis of the rest space of that observer. Neither existence of a
tetrad field on a prescribed open set, nor global existence on $M$, is
asserted by this definition; local existence near every point is proved in the
existence theorem on this page.

**(d) Observer-adapted tetrads.** Given an observer $n$ at a point $p$, a
tetrad at $p$ is **$n$-adapted** when its first member is $n$. Given an
observer congruence $n$ on $U$, a tetrad field on $U$ is
**$n$-adapted** when $E_0=n$; its remaining members are then $g$-orthonormal
fields in the moving rest spaces of the congruence.

**(e) Scope.** A tetrad field is not assumed to be a coordinate frame, and a
frame field is not assumed to be orthonormal. Components of a tensor field in a
tetrad and components in a chart are different objects; the transformation
rules for the two are distinguished later on this page. No relation to the
physical interpretation of a reference frame is asserted here beyond the
geometric data listed above.
items.strategy: Define frame fields as pointwise bases of smooth fields, distinguish coordinate frames by the commuting necessary condition, and define tetrad and adapted tetrad fields by orthonormality and the first-member condition.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases': the vielbeins with g_mu nu e^mu_a e^nu_b = eta_ab (3.118)-(3.119) and the orthonormal-frame components, printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 95-98)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.2: orthonormal bases at a point and the Lorentz transformations between them (2.9)-(2.10), printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 2.3.3 on tensors and tensor fields, printed pp. 72-75 (PDF pp. 79-82)

items.title: The change between two future-directed tetrads is a Lorentz matrix
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ and $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2,F_3)$ be two
future-directed tetrads at $p$ ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Then there is a unique real
$4\times4$ matrix $\Lambda=(\Lambda^B{}_A)$ such that
$F_A=\sum_B\Lambda^B{}_AE_B$ for all $A$, and:

1. $\sum_{C,D}\Lambda^C{}_A\,\eta_{CD}\,\Lambda^D{}_B=\eta_{AB}$ for all
   $A,B$; equivalently $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$.
2. $\Lambda$ is invertible and $\det\Lambda=\pm1$.
3. $\Lambda^0{}_0>0$.
4. For every covariant $2$-tensor $T$ at $p$, its components in the two
   tetrads satisfy
   $T(F_A,F_B)=\sum_{C,D}\Lambda^C{}_A\Lambda^D{}_BT(E_C,E_D)$.
   More generally, for a type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ each contravariant slot
   contributes a factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^A{}_B$ and each covariant slot a
   factor $\Lambda^A{}_B$.
items.strategy: Write one tetrad in the basis of the other, evaluate the metric on both sides to obtain the Lorentz matrix identity, take determinants, and locate the time-time entry through the future-cone coordinate description.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases', printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 95-98)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.2: different orthonormal bases are related by Lorentz transformations, eta_mu nu = (A^-1)^rho_mu (A^-1)^sigma_nu eta_rho sigma (2.9)-(2.10), printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29)

items.title: Existence of a smooth future-directed tetrad field near every event
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Then there is an open
neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ of $p$ and a smooth future-directed tetrad field
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ on $U$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]), i.e.
$g_q(E_A(q),E_B(q))=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$ for all $q\in U$ with
$E_0(q)$ future-directed for every $q\in U$.
items.strategy: Construct the tetrad from constant-coefficient fields of a future orthonormal basis at the point, then normalize and orthogonalize inside the rest space with successive shrinking; smoothness of the square root and reciprocal is supplied by the injective-regular-map theorem and the derivative rules.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases', printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 95-98)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.2: an orthonormal basis of the tangent space exists at every point and any two are related by a Lorentz transformation, printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.1.2: an orthonormal basis of T_pM can always be found at each point, printed p. 93 (PDF p. 100)

items.title: Relative velocity decomposition of a future unit timelike vector
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, let $n$ be an observer at $p$, let $c>0$ be a real parameter, and let
$u\in T_pM$ be future unit timelike, $g_p(u,u)=-1$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Put

$$\gamma:=-g_p(n,u),\qquad w:=\frac{c\,h_n(u)}{\gamma},$$

where $h_n$ is the spatial projection. Then:

1. $\gamma\ge1$, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$; in particular
   $w$ is well defined.
2. $w\in n^{\perp}$, $g_p(w,w)=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})<c^2$, and

   $$u=\gamma\left(n+\frac{w}{c}\right).$$

3. **Uniqueness.** If $u=\lambda(n+v/c)$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
   $v\in n^{\perp}$, then $\lambda=\gamma$ and $v=w$.
4. **Converse.** Conversely, if $\lambda\ge1$ and $v\in n^{\perp}$ satisfy
   $g_p(v,v)=c^2(1-\lambda^{-2})$, then $u':=\lambda(n+v/c)$ is future unit
   timelike, $-g_p(n,u')=\lambda$ and $h_n(u')=\lambda v/c$; the maps
   $u\mapsto(\gamma,w)$ and $(\lambda,v)\mapsto u'$ are mutually inverse
   bijections between the future unit timelike vectors and the pairs
   $(\lambda,v)$ with $\lambda\ge1$, $v\in n^{\perp}$ and
   $g_p(v,v)=c^2(1-\lambda^{-2})$.
items.strategy: Decompose a future unit timelike vector in the observer's orthogonal direct sum, use the projection identity and positivity for gamma greater or equal 1, and prove uniqueness and the converse by pairing with the observer.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'Lorentz transformations' and the Lorentz factor (printed pp. 4-6; PDF pp. 11-13) and 'four-velocity' U^mu = dx^mu/dtau with eta_mu nu U^mu U^nu = -1 (1.98)-(1.99), printed pp. 26-27 (PDF pp. 33-34)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 2.3: the 4-velocity as the unit tangent of a timelike curve, g_ab u^a u^b = -1 (2.14), printed p. 28 (PDF p. 29), and section 6.3: the observer energy E = -g_ab(p) v^a(p) P^b(p) (6.19), printed p. 64 (PDF p. 65)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), Ch. 5, section 5.3: the orthogonal decomposition u = Gamma(n + U) of a 4-velocity with respect to an observer, with n.U = 0 and Gamma = (1 - U.U)^-1/2 (5.29)-(5.36), printed pp. 76-77

items.title: Every congruence admits a local adapted chart
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, let $n$ be an observer congruence on
$U$, and let $p\in U$
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). Then there is a chart
$(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ of $M$ with domain $U'\subseteq U$ containing $p$ such
that

$$n=\frac{\partial}{\partial u^0}\qquad\text{on }U',$$

and this chart is $n$-adapted: its spatial coordinates $u^1,u^2,u^3$ are
constant along every integral curve of $n$ contained in $U'$.
items.strategy: Apply the flow-box theorem to the nowhere-vanishing congruence field, rename coordinates so the field is the first coordinate field, and read adaptness off the constancy of spatial coordinates along the flow.

references.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 9 'Integral Curves and Flows': flows and the canonical form of a flow (the flow box theorem), printed pp. 206-222

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), Ch. 4, section 4.2: coordinates adapted to the foliation, with x^0 = const. on the leaves, printed pp. 54-59

items.title: Smoothness of the rest-space family and its Frobenius integrability criterion
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, and let $n$ be an observer
congruence on $U$ ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]). Let
$\alpha:=n^{\flat}\in\Omega^1(U)$ be the smooth $1$-form
$\alpha_q(v)=g_q(n_q,v)$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]), and let
$\mathcal D_q:=\ker\alpha_q=\{v\in T_qM:g_q(n_q,v)=0\}=n_q^{\perp}$ be the
rest space of the congruence at $q$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Then:

1. $\alpha$ is nowhere zero on $U$, and $q\mapsto\mathcal D_q$ is a smooth
   rank-$3$ distribution on $U$
   ([[def-smooth-distribution-on-a-manifold]]).
2. $\mathcal D$ is integrable
   ([[def-integrable-distribution]]) if and only if
   $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on $U$
   ([[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]],
   [[def-wedge-product-of-differential-forms]]).
3. If $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on $U$, then every point of $U$ has a chart
   $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ in which
   $\mathcal D=\operatorname{span}(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$;
   equivalently, the rest spaces are tangent to the level hypersurfaces of
   $u^0$.
items.strategy: Show that the flat of the congruence is a nowhere-zero smooth one-form, frame its kernel locally by explicit chart fields, and apply the codimension-one Frobenius criterion and the local coordinate theorem.

references.title: J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 'Distributions and Foliations': distributions and involutivity (printed pp. 491-496) and the Frobenius theorem (printed pp. 496-501)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), Ch. 2, sections 2.3-2.4: hypersurfaces, the use of the Frobenius theorem for tangency of the commutator of tangent vectors (printed pp. 23-28), and Ch. 3, sections 3.3.3-3.3.4: the congruence of Eulerian observers is hypersurface-orthogonal and has vanishing vorticity (printed pp. 42-44)

items.title: Observer-relative energy, spatial momentum and rest mass of a tangent vector
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, let $n$ be an observer at $p$, and let $c>0$ be a real parameter
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observer energy and spatial momentum.** For every $P\in T_pM$ define the
**observer energy** and the **spatial momentum** of $P$ relative to $n$ by

$$E_n(P):=-c\,g_p(P,n),\qquad q_n(P):=h_n(P),$$

where $h_n$ is the spatial projection of the observer $n$. Both maps are
$\mathbb R$-linear in $P$: the first because $g_p$ is bilinear, the second by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The second takes values in the
rest space $n^{\perp}$, and by the rest-space decomposition of that lemma every
$P$ has the unique decomposition

$$P=\frac{E_n(P)}{c}\,n+q_n(P),\qquad \frac{E_n(P)}{c}\in\mathbb R,\quad q_n(P)\in n^{\perp}.$$

Equivalently $E_n(P)=c\,\lambda$ and $q_n(P)=w$ for the unique pair
$(\lambda,w)$ with $P=\lambda n+w$, $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $w\in n^{\perp}$.

**(b) Rest mass and four-velocity normalization.** For $P\in T_pM$ with
$g_p(P,P)\le0$ define the **rest mass**

$$m(P):=\frac{\sqrt{-g_p(P,P)}}{c}\ge0,$$

where the square root is the nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]. By
strict positivity of the square root of a positive number, $m(P)=0$ exactly
when $P=0$ or $P$ is null, and $m(P)>0$ exactly when $P$ is timelike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). When $m(P)>0$, define the
**normalized four-velocity direction**

$$U(P):=\frac{P}{m(P)},$$

so that $g_p(U(P),U(P))=g_p(P,P)/m(P)^2=-c^2$. Conversely, if $m>0$ and
$U\in T_pM$ satisfy $g_p(U,U)=-c^2$, then $P:=mU$ has $g_p(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ and
$m(P)=m$, $U(P)=U$; the pair $(m,U)$ with $U$ future-directed determines and
is determined by its future timelike $P=mU$.

**(c) Scope and reading.** $E_n$ and $q_n$ depend on the observer $n$: for the
same nonzero $P$, different observers $n,n'$ generally give different values,
and no observer-independent splitting of $P$ into "energy" and "momentum" is
defined by this item. The identities above are algebraic; this definition
asserts no positivity of $E_n$ (that is proved separately), no conservation,
no dynamics and no measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum
and rest mass, and their physical units and interpretation, belong to the
physical reading of the framework's unit conventions and postulates and are
not asserted here; this item fixes only the mathematical dependence on the
objects $P$, $n$, $g_p$ and the parameter $c$.
items.strategy: Define observer energy and spatial momentum as the linear maps minus c g(P,n) and h_n(P), record the unique decomposition of P, and define rest mass and normalized four-velocity from g(P,P) with the nonnegative square root; physical units and readings are deferred.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 on four-momentum, energy and the mass shell, printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 33-35)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.3 on four-momentum, mass and observer energy, printed pp. 63-65 (PDF pp. 64-66)

items.title: Positivity, relative-velocity identities and the mass shell of observer-relative energy and momentum
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, let $n$ be an observer at $p$, let $c>0$, and for
$P\in T_pM$ write $E:=E_n(P)$, $q:=q_n(P)$ and $m:=m(P)$ as in
[[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]. Then:

1. **Master identity.** $E^2=c^2\bigl(g_p(q,q)-g_p(P,P)\bigr)$.
2. **Positivity.** If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E>0$.
3. **Mass shell.** If $P$ is future timelike, then $m>0$ and, with
   $U:=P/m$, $u:=U/c$ and $\gamma:=-g_p(n,u)$, one has $\gamma\ge1$,
   $E=mc^2\gamma$, $q=m\gamma w$ where $w:=c\,h_n(u)/\gamma$,
   $g_p(q,q)=m^2c^2(\gamma^2-1)$ and

   $$E^2=m^2c^4+c^2g_p(q,q).$$
4. **Null case.** If $P$ is future null and nonzero, then $E>0$,
   $E=c\sqrt{g_p(q,q)}$ and $E^2=c^2g_p(q,q)$.
items.strategy: Use the decomposition of P for the master identity, the observer pairing lemma for positivity, and the relative-velocity theorem to evaluate the mass shell; the null case follows by specialization.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1, equations (1.98)-(1.102) on four-momentum, energy and the mass shell, printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 33-35)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.3, equations (6.17)-(6.19) on P = m u, g(P,P) = -m^2 and observer energy, printed pp. 63-65 (PDF pp. 64-66)

items.title: Charts, frames, tetrads, congruences and observers are distinct objects
items.statement:
This page introduces several objects that are related but not interchangeable;
the distinctions below are part of their definitions and are used throughout
the general-relativity track.

- **Observer.** An observer at $p$ is one future-directed unit timelike vector
  $n\in T_pM$, $g_p(n,n)=-1$
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). It carries no parametrized curve and no
  clock reading by itself.
- **Congruence.** An observer congruence on an open set $U$ is a smooth field
  $n$ whose value at every point is an observer; its maximal integral curves
  are its observer curves, and its flow parameter is not a physical time
  ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
- **Frame and coordinate frame.** A local frame field is a tuple of four
  pointwise independent smooth vector fields; the coordinate frame of a smooth
  chart is the special case of the fields $\partial/\partial x^a$, whose
  members pairwise commute. A frame whose members do not commute is therefore
  not the coordinate frame of any chart
  ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
- **Tetrad.** A tetrad field is a pointwise $g$-orthonormal frame field; it is
  future-directed when its first member is future-directed, and it is adapted
  to a congruence $n$ when that first member equals $n$. A tetrad field need
  not be a coordinate frame. Local existence near every point is proved on this
  page; global existence on $M$ is not asserted and would be a nontrivial
  parallelizability property of the manifold.
- **Adapted chart.** A chart is $n$-adapted when its spatial coordinates are
  constant along the integral curves of $n$; one exists near every point of a
  congruence, by the existence corollary on this page, but it is not unique and
  its coordinate field need not equal $n$
  ([[cor-gr-adapted-chart-existence]]).
- **Rest spaces and their integrability.** The rest spaces $n_q^{\perp}$ of a
  congruence always form a smooth rank-$3$ distribution, and they are tangent
  to local hypersurfaces exactly when $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ for
  $\alpha=n^{\flat}$. Thus an adapted chart always exists, while an orthogonal
  rest-space foliation need not
  ([[prop-gr-rest-space-integrability-criterion]]).
- **Components.** Coordinate components of a tensor field transform by
  products of chart Jacobians
  ([[lem-gr-tensor-component-transformation-law]]), while its components in
  two future-directed tetrads are related by a matrix
  $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$ and
  $\Lambda^0{}_0>0$ ([[lem-gr-tetrad-change-of-basis-is-lorentz]]). The two
  component systems are different data
  ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).
- **Observer-relative quantities.** Observer energy, spatial momentum and
  rest mass are defined with respect to a chosen observer; different observers
  generally assign different energies to the same tangent vector, and no
  observer-independent split of a tangent vector into energy and momentum is
  asserted ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]).
- **Physical readings.** The interpretation of these geometric objects as
  observers, reference frames, clocks, particles and measured energies belongs
  to the physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework, recorded
  elsewhere on this track; the items on this page assert no measurement,
  dynamics or claim about nature.
items.strategy: Bookkeeping remark distinguishing observer, congruence, frame, tetrad, adapted chart, rest-space integrability and observer-relative quantities, with pointers to the items that prove each property.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), sections 1.7-1.8 on tensor components and tensor fields, printed pp. 16-21 (PDF pp. 17-22), and section 2.2 on orthonormal bases and Lorentz transformations between them, printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 27-29)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2 'coordinate bases' and 'the tensor transformation law' (printed pp. 45-47; PDF pp. 52-54) and Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases' (printed pp. 88-91; PDF pp. 95-98)

items.title: A mixed tensor field: components in two charts and the invariance of its trace
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the flat Lorentzian metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the time orientation $N=\partial_0$, so
that $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]); here $g$ and $N$ enter only to place
the charts and the tensor field in the setting of the cited definition and
take no part in the computation. Let $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be the identity
chart and let the chart $y=(y^0,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ be defined by

$$y^0=x^0,\qquad y^1=x^1+x^0,\qquad y^2=x^2,\qquad y^3=x^3 .$$

Define a type $(1,1)$ tensor field $T$ on $M$ by its components in the $x$
chart,

$$T^0{}_1:=1,\qquad T^2{}_3:=x^1,\qquad T^a{}_b:=0\text{ otherwise}.$$

Then $T$ is a smooth type $(1,1)$ tensor field. Its components in the chart
$y$ are

$$T'^0{}_0=-1,\quad T'^0{}_1=1,\quad T'^1{}_0=-1,\quad T'^1{}_1=1,\quad T'^2{}_3=y^1-y^0,\quad\text{others }0,$$

and its trace computed in the two charts agrees: it is $0$ in both, as the
chart-independence of contraction requires.
items.strategy: Compute the affine chart change and its constant Jacobians, transform a mixed tensor's components by the component law, and compare its traces in the two charts.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2 'the tensor transformation law' (printed pp. 46-47; PDF pp. 53-54) and Ch. 1 'index manipulation' (printed pp. 17-19; PDF pp. 24-26)
J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 12 'Tensors and Tensor Fields on Manifolds', printed pp. 316-324

items.title: A constant boosted tetrad field on flat spacetime and an adapted chart
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and the
flat Lorentzian metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with time
orientation $N=\partial_0$. Let $\beta\in(-1,1)$ and let
$\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}>0$. Define the constant-coefficient fields

$$E_0:=\gamma(\partial_0+\beta\partial_1),\qquad E_1:=\gamma(\beta\partial_0+\partial_1),\qquad E_2:=\partial_2,\qquad E_3:=\partial_3 .$$

Then $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ is a smooth future-directed tetrad field on $M$, and
$n:=E_0$ is an observer congruence whose integral curves have
$x^1-\beta x^0$, $x^2$ and $x^3$ constant; hence
$u:=(x^0,\,x^1-\beta x^0,\,x^2,\,x^3)$ is an $n$-adapted chart. In that chart
$n=\gamma\,\partial_{u^0}$, so the coordinate field of an adapted chart need
not equal the congruence.
items.strategy: Verify that the constant boosted fields are smooth, orthonormal and future-directed, and exhibit an adapted chart for the resulting parallel congruence with an explicit inverse.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'Lorentz transformations' including boosts (printed pp. 5-7; PDF pp. 12-14) and 'four-velocity' (printed pp. 26-27; PDF pp. 33-34)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 1.9 on integral curves (printed pp. 21-22; PDF pp. 22-23) and section 2.3 on the 4-velocity (2.14) (printed p. 28; PDF p. 29)

items.title: A shearing observer congruence on flat spacetime: tetrad, adapted chart and non-coordinate frame
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ carry the identity chart $x$ and the flat Lorentzian metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ with time orientation $N=\partial_0$. Fix
$\lambda>0$ and put

$$W:=\{(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):\lvert\lambda x^1\rvert<1/2\},\qquad \Omega:=\lambda x^1,\qquad \gamma:=(1-\Omega^2)^{-1/2}>0 .$$

Define the smooth fields on $W$

$$E_0:=\gamma(\partial_0+\Omega\partial_2),\quad E_1:=\partial_1,\quad E_2:=\gamma(\Omega\partial_0+\partial_2),\quad E_3:=\partial_3 .$$

Then $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ is a future-directed tetrad field on $W$, its first
member $n:=E_0$ is an observer congruence, the chart
$u:=(x^0,\,x^1,\,x^2-\Omega(x^1)x^0,\,x^3)$ is $n$-adapted with
$\partial_{u^0}=n/\gamma$, and the tetrad is not the coordinate frame of any
chart, because
$[E_0,E_1]=-\gamma'\partial_0-(\gamma\Omega)'\partial_2$ is nonzero at every
point of $W$ with $x^1\neq0$, where $\gamma'=\gamma^3\lambda^2x^1$.
items.strategy: Construct the shearing congruence and its tetrad from a positive smooth gamma, verify orthonormality, produce an explicit adapted chart with inverse, and compute the bracket showing the frame is not a coordinate frame.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases' (printed pp. 88-91; PDF pp. 95-98) and Ch. 4 'physics in curved spacetime' (printed pp. 104-106; PDF pp. 111-113)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 1.9 on integral curves (printed pp. 21-22; PDF pp. 22-23)

items.title: The relative-velocity decomposition of a boost, checked in an explicit tetrad
items.statement:
Let $(\mathbb R^4,g)$ and the constant boosted tetrad field
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be as in [[ex-gr-boosted-constant-tetrad-field]], with
$E_0=n$ future unit timelike, $E_1$ unit spacelike and $g(E_0,E_1)=0$. Let
$\beta\in(-1,1)$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $c>0$, and set

$$w:=\beta c\,E_1,\qquad u:=\gamma\Bigl(n+\frac{w}{c}\Bigr)=\gamma(E_0+\beta E_1).$$

Then $u$ is future unit timelike, $-g(n,u)=\gamma\ge1$, $h_n(u)=\gamma\beta E_1$,
$w=c\,h_n(u)/\gamma$, and $g(w,w)=\beta^2c^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})<c^2$ whenever
$\beta\neq0$. This verifies the relative-velocity decomposition theorem of the
tensors page in an explicit family.
items.strategy: Evaluate the relative-velocity theorem on the explicit family u = gamma(n + beta E_1), computing the metric, gamma and the spatial projection directly.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 'Lorentz transformations' and the Lorentz factor (printed pp. 4-6; PDF pp. 11-13) and 'four-velocity' (1.98)-(1.99) (printed pp. 26-27; PDF pp. 33-34)

E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), Ch. 5, section 5.3: the orthogonal decomposition u = Gamma(n + U) and Gamma = (1 - U.U)^-1/2 (5.29)-(5.36), printed pp. 76-77

items.title: Observer energy, spatial momentum and mass shell of a boosted test body
items.statement:
Keep the setting of [[ex-gr-observer-relative-velocity-of-a-boost]]: the flat
metric $g$ on $\mathbb R^4$, the tetrad $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$, the observer
$n=E_0$, the parameters $\beta\in(-1,1)$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $c>0$,
and the future unit timelike vector $u=\gamma(E_0+\beta E_1)$ with
$g(u,u)=-1$ and $-g(n,u)=\gamma$. Let $m>0$ and set

$$P:=mc\,u.$$

Then $P$ is future timelike, its rest mass is $m(P)=m$, and relative to the
observer $n$ its energy and spatial momentum are

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad q_n(P)=mc\gamma\beta\,E_1,$$

so that $g(q_n(P),q_n(P))=m^2c^2\gamma^2\beta^2$ and the mass shell
$E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2g(q_n(P),q_n(P))$ holds. This is the standard boosted
test-body kinematics in the abstract observer split.
items.strategy: Compute rest mass, energy and momentum of P = mc u in the explicit boosted tetrad and verify the mass-shell identity.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 1 on four-momentum, energy and the mass shell, printed pp. 26-28 (PDF pp. 33-35)
H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.3, equations (6.17)-(6.19) on P = m u, g(P,P) = -m^2 and observer energy, printed pp. 63-65 (PDF pp. 64-66)

items.title: A tetrad field that is not the coordinate frame of any chart
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "every smooth future-directed tetrad field on a nonempty
open subset of flat Lorentzian four-space is the coordinate frame of some
smooth chart" ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
items.strategy: Refute the universal coordinate-frame claim with the shearing tetrad, whose nonvanishing bracket contradicts the commuting necessary condition.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 3 'tetrads and non-coordinate bases', printed pp. 88-91 (PDF pp. 95-98)
J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 8 'Vector Fields': Lie brackets and the commuting of coordinate vector fields, printed pp. 185-189

items.title: A congruence whose rest spaces are not tangent to any local hypersurfaces
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "for every observer congruence on a nonempty open subset of
flat Lorentzian four-space, the family of rest spaces is tangent to local
hypersurfaces" ([[prop-gr-rest-space-integrability-criterion]]).
items.strategy: Refute universal integrability of rest spaces by computing alpha wedge d alpha for the shearing congruence and applying the Frobenius criterion.

references.title: E. Gourgoulhon, 3+1 Formalism and Bases of Numerical Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/0703035 (2007), Ch. 2, sections 2.3-2.4: hypersurface-orthogonality and the Frobenius theorem in the proof that the Weingarten map preserves the tangent space (printed pp. 23-28); Ch. 3, section 3.3.3: a hypersurface-orthogonal congruence of Eulerian observers has vanishing vorticity (printed p. 44)
J. M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed., Ch. 19 'Distributions and Foliations': the Frobenius theorem, printed pp. 491-501
